items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: There was a gambling house on 5th Street between John and Central Avenue which was run by a man named Ed Gaither.

ctx.x: When the dances started, I always managed to have a ring side standing spot and a girl was playing trumpet. The saxophone player was the leader and the group was known as Clarence Page and His Syncopators. The girl playing the trumpet was Dolly Jones and it was her and her mother that I had seen going down Hathaway Street with trumpet cases and later heard them blowing. I was fascinated by Dolly's playing and she seemed at home with the rest of the musicians. A girl playing in an orchestra with men had never been…

Clarence Page played in the Sterling Hotel in the winter. The Sterling was on 6th and Mound Streets and had been a big time white hotel at one time. More and more negro people started to come to Cincinnati from the Southern states and this part of the city called Downtown was where they found homes and places of entertainment. There was a gambling house on 5th Street between John and Central Avenue which was run by a man named Ed Gaither. He later opened another one in Carlisle Avenue and Mount Street. My mother…

The Sterling Hotel had big dances in the winter and I could hear the music coming from the ballroom from outside, but it was not as interesting as in the summer when Clarence would play in Sinton Park.
